title: Request-anchor checkpointing for low-overhead span correlation across async fanout
creator: Rohit Menon
description:
Problem: Long-lived requests, streaming responses, and high-fanout worker patterns cause trace fragmentation and KV cache churn. Current span stitching relies on carrying full trace envelopes between services which increases header size and is brittle when parts of the request cross language or protocol boundaries. We need a lightweight, SDK-level primitive that creates stable, compact 'anchor' markers at the ingress boundary and uses an optional short-lived KV lease so downstream slices (workers, async jobs, edge proxies) can attach spans to the same logical request without exchanging the full trace envelope.

Goals:
- Provide a tiny, language-agnostic anchor ID that can be emitted in a single short header or message attribute (~<= 50 bytes).
- Ensure anchor IDs are backward-compatible fallbacks to standard trace IDs (no loss of observability if the feature is off).
- Reduce header/baggage bloat while preserving end-to-end correlation across fanout, workers, and streaming responses.
- Align sampling decisions across attached services using a short-lived KV lease (TTL 30s-5m) that stores sampling hints and minimal provenance.

Scope:
- Add "anchorCheckpoint()" primitive to Node/Python/Go SDKs and middleware for Express/FastAPI/gRPC interceptors.
- Implement lightweight server-side stitcher middleware in runtime that resolves anchor -> trace mapping using new KV-lease API and attaches downstream spans to the originating trace.
- Add diagnostic metrics and a dashboard showing anchor issuance rate, lease hit/miss, stitch success rate, and overhead latency.
- Provide a feature-flagged rollout with opt-in via headers or SDK config.

Non-goals:
- This ticket does not change core sampling algorithms or long-term storage of spans. It focuses on short-lived correlation to improve trace continuity and reduce header size.
acceptance_criteria: SDKs provide anchorCheckpoint() and middleware examples for Node/Python/Go
End-to-end traces for a representative fanout pipeline show >95% successful stitch (anchor->trace) in canary traffic
Median additional latency at SDK ingress & stitcher is < 1ms; p95 < 5ms in baseline perf tests
Header/baggage size for correlated requests reduced by >= 70% compared to current full-envelope carry
Dashboard panels for anchor issuance, lease hit/miss, stitch success, and CPU/latency overhead exist and update in real-time
Feature gated by runtime flag and opt-in SDK config; rolling back the flag restores previous behaviour with no trace loss
notes: 2026-02-26: Spike completed — prototype anchor format chosen: base62(48-bit timestamp + 64-bit random) -> ~16 bytes text. Draft design doc created.
2026-03-01: Node SDK PoC implemented (middleware + simple express example). Initial microbench shows ~0.6ms median overhead on ingress path.
2026-03-04: Discussed lease TTL tradeoffs with infra: default 60s, configurable per-request. Short TTL reduces lease churn but increases miss probability for long fanouts.
2026-03-06: Opened implementation PR for runtime stitcher: GH: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4621 (WIP).
2026-03-08: Benchmark run on staging: 10k req/s simulated fanout of 4 workers. Anchor lease hit rate 93% with default TTL; memory overhead negligible.
2026-03-10: Security reviewed header attack surface; decided to HMAC anchor IDs with deployment key for internal validation (configurable).
